body_html:
How it works

Mathematics is the study of patterns. Famous sequences: odd numbers 1, 3, 5, …; triangular numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, …; square numbers 1, 4, 9, 16, …; powers of 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, ….

Adding odd numbers gives squares: 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 = 3 × 3. Adding counting numbers gives triangular numbers: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.

In the Virahanka numbers 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, … each number is the sum of the two before it.

Example

Find 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11.

Six odd numbers

6 × 6

Answer: 36

Example

What comes next: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …?

Add 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6

Answer: 21

Common mistakes

  • Adding the same step to a pattern that grows faster, like the squares.
  • Thinking 6 × 6 is 12 (that is 6 + 6).
  • Mixing up triangular numbers (1, 3, 6, 10) and square numbers (1, 4, 9, 16).

faq.a: Numbers of dots that make a triangle: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, … — the sums 1 + 2 + … + n.

faq.q: Why does adding odd numbers give square numbers?
faq.a: Each odd number adds an L-shaped border to a square of dots, making the next square.
The sequence 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, … where each number is the sum of the two before it; Virahanka described it centuries before Fibonacci.
